$comment: Launcher manifest for the more-leaves mod. Like every content mod this file only DESCRIBES the mod; the value store is the live %LOCALAPPDATA%\LeafItAloneSafe\more-leaves.json that apply.ps1 seeds and reads, and apply/revert run the validated scripts. Adding a mod means writing a manifest like this, never new launcher UI code. This is the L7 proof: a second UnityPy mod discovered with zero launcher changes.
name: More leaves per area
description: Makes leaf areas denser so there are more leaves to rake before you unload. Per world it raises every coupled leaf count by the same factor - the scatter-position bank (each position expanded IN PLACE so each area keeps its own block of spots), the scene spawn budget (which also sets the completion goal) and the runtime leaf-area layout that decides how many leaves are actually pickable - so the extra leaves both appear AND can be collected at any multiplier. The title-screen backdrop shares the Hometown bank, so it scales with Hometown and stays whole.

fields.label: Hometown density
fields.help: Integer factor on Hometown's leaf spawn budget, scatter-position bank AND runtime pickable-leaf layout. 1 = leave vanilla, 2 = twice as many leaves, etc.

fields.label: Castle density
fields.help: Integer factor on Castle's leaf spawn budget, scatter-position bank AND runtime pickable-leaf layout. 1 = leave vanilla.

fields.label: Sakura density
fields.help: Integer factor on Sakura's leaf spawn budget, scatter-position bank AND runtime pickable-leaf layout. 1 = leave vanilla.

fields.label: Scatter radius (m)
fields.help: How far (metres, x/z) an added leaf is nudged from an existing spot. 0 stacks them; ~0.6 spreads them into the nearby grass. Leaf height is always preserved.

$patchesComment: 2b conflict detection (from patch_leaves/prefab/positions/areas.py): more-leaves grows one coupled leaf budget in lockstep across every source that must agree, so it writes the Area layout's leavesCount + initArgs[].leavesCount in each gameplay scene bundle (and the title-screen menu scene), the same layout in the coreprefabs actor template, the areas registry count, and the InitialLeaves scatter-position bank. All in leaf/scene bundles - none in coreassets_assets_scenes - so it does not collide with sakura-petals-everywhere (which edits the scene-definition material).
